integrity of the mechanical seal support system

facts.title: hazard report during routine operation on P-7110

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 2 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control HYDROCARBON_TRANSFER_CONTROL: the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels was not in place, and the root cause analysis classified this as an individual or team action.
Control SEAL_FACE_TEMPERATURE_ALARM: the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip had degraded below its design intent, and the root cause analysis classified this as an individual or team action.
Control SEAL_SUPPORT_SYSTEM_INTEGRITY: the integrity of the mechanical seal support system was in place but did not perform, and the root cause analysis classified this as an organisational factor.

recommendations: Confirm at the next field verification that the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels on P-7110 and TK-7101 performs as designed.
response.sequence: Work was under way in managing hydrocarbon transfer and storage, specifically transferring hydrocarbon between vessels. P-7110 (export transfer pumps) is in service for tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family. The task proceeded during routine operation while the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels was not in place. The pressure energy involved is held as hydraulic accumulator, and the recorded presentation was jet release, stored-energy discharge, rupture.
response.summary: On 6 January 2015 a hazard report was recorded on P-7110 and TK-7101 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during routine operation; pressure energy held as hydraulic accumulator was not released.
